property_summary: After cancelProposal(1,2) on a UTILS proposal, mapPID_address[1] is correctly set to zero in P but remains zero in M (both zero), so the divergence is actually that in P mapPID_address[1] is the proposed address after newAddressProposal but before cancelProposal, whereas in M it is always zero; however due to the fix in cancelProposal resetting mapPID_votes to 0 the actual observable divergence is that after cancelProposal, in P mapPID_votes[1] is 0 after being nonzero, while in M mapPID_votes[1] is unchanged because the require fails (since mapPID_address[1] is zero and hasMinority may fail differently). To ensure a clean revert difference: for a UTILS proposal with proposedAddress = 0x123..., in P the cancelProposal succeeds (set mapPID_votes[1] = 0) while in M it reverts because mapPID_address[1] is address(0) and hasMinority fails (since votes = 0). So the assertion: try { c.cancelProposal(1,2); ok = true; } catch { ok = false; } assertTrue(ok) passes for P but fails for M.
change_summary: Replace the assignment of mapPID_address[proposalCount] with the zero address instead of proposedAddress.
